manual.title: Connect with an MA API token
manual.description:
Connect HOMEii Music Flow 6 to Music Assistant.

1. Open Music Assistant → Settings → Profile → Long-lived access tokens. Create a token named HOMEii Flow Engine and copy it. This must be a Music Assistant token, not a Home Assistant token or Spotify API key.
2. Enter the direct MA server URL below (usually port 8095), not your HA dashboard or ingress URL.
3. Paste the token and submit. The connection is checked before saving.
4. Once the Engine is loaded, add or upgrade the HOMEii Music Flow card.

[Open the illustrated MA token guide](https://www.music-assistant.io/settings/profile/). The guide is documentation; open your own MA installation to create the token.

For a normal installation, leave both identifiers as default.

data_description.music_assistant_url: Direct Music Assistant server address reachable from Home Assistant, usually port 8095. Example: http://192.168.1.100:8095. Do not enter your HA dashboard URL.
data_description.music_assistant_external_url: Optional HTTPS Web Server/API URL used for artwork when the internal address is unavailable. Do not use the Home Assistant ingress page.
data_description.music_assistant_token: MA → Settings → Profile → Long-lived access tokens → create a token named HOMEii Flow Engine. Paste it here. Keep it private; it is stored in HA and not included in card YAML.
data_description.instance_id: Identifies this Engine connection inside Home Assistant. Leave default for one Engine. Use a unique ID only when deliberately creating a separate Engine instance; cards can select that same ID. This is not a speaker name or an MA user ID.
data_description.profile_id: Default namespace for Engine policies and stored schedules. Leave default for normal use. It is not your Music Assistant login/profile. Cards using a custom Engine profile must use the matching profile ID.

automatic.title: Sign in to Music Assistant
automatic.description: Use a local Music Assistant username and password, not your Home Assistant login. Submitting creates a dedicated token named HOMEii Flow Engine. Your password is used only for this request and is not saved. If you only sign in through Home Assistant, go back and choose manual token setup.
